full_text_en:
Sun Aiqin — Introducing Bribes

Procuratorial Authority: Jingkou District People's Procuratorate of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province

Defendant: Sun Aiqin, male, 47 years old, formerly Deputy Director of the Zhenjiang City Urban Construction Comprehensive Development Leading Group Office and concurrently Director of the Demolition and Relocation Affairs Office, detained on June 21, 2001, in connection with this case

Defense Counsel: Zhou Yuzheng and Rong Haojun, lawyers from Nanjing Sanfa Law Firm

The Jingkou District People's Procuratorate of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, filed a public prosecution with the Jingkou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City against the defendant Sun Aiqin for the crimes of bribery and bribery by company personnel.

The indictment alleged: In April 1993, during the joint development of the plot at No. 8 Jiankang Road between Zhenjiang City Supply and Marketing Cooperative Real Estate Development Company (now Shenlong Real Estate Development Company, a collectively-owned enterprise, hereinafter "Supply and Marketing Company") and Liu Yijiang, who was affiliated with Zhenjiang City Zhenhua Housing Development Company (hereinafter "Zhenhua Company"), the defendant Sun Aiqin, together with Zhu Jinshun, Deputy Manager of Supply and Marketing Company, and others, used Zhu Jinshun's official position to jointly accept a bribe of RMB 200,000 from Liu Yijiang, of which Sun Aiqin appropriated RMB 50,000 for himself. In June 1994, Dantu County Real Estate Administration Bureau of Zhenjiang City (hereinafter "Dantu Real Estate Bureau") jointly developed the plot at No. 17 Jiankang Road with Liu Yijiang. During this process, Sun Aiqin, together with Zhou Wei, Director of Dantu Real Estate Bureau, used Zhou Wei's official position to jointly accept a bribe of RMB 100,000 from Liu Yijiang, with each receiving RMB 50,000; thereafter, Sun Aiqin individually accepted a bribe of RMB 80,000 from Liu Yijiang. The act of Sun Aiqin jointly accepting bribes with Zhu Jinshun and others violated Article 163 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and constituted the crime of bribery by company personnel; the acts of Sun Aiqin jointly accepting bribes with Zhou Wei and individually accepting a bribe from Liu Yijiang violated Article 385 of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of bribery. Sun Aiqin committed two crimes and should be subject to concurrent punishment for multiple crimes. The procuratorate requested a judgment according to law.

The procuratorial authority submitted the following evidence to the court:

1. Testimony of witness Liu Yijiang, mainly to the effect: At the end of 1993, while I was affiliated with Zhenhua Company, I obtained the approval document for the plot at No. 8 Jiankang Road from the military through a comrade-in-arms. There was a small two-story building on this land that needed to be demolished. I got to know Sun Aiqin because he, as the then-Director of the Demolition Office, helped with the demolition. Since I lacked the qualifications and capability to develop this land, I asked Sun Aiqin to find a strong developer to transfer the project. The condition was that, aside from the land cost, I would pay a transfer fee of RMB 500,000, and Sun agreed. Sun first contacted Lu Guangyu from Jingjing Development Company, but since Lu could not make decisions, Sun then contacted Zhu Jinshun from Zhenhua Company. At first, I authorized Sun Aiqin and Lu Guangyu to negotiate with Zhu Jinshun, and the total land price was set at RMB 2.5 million, a figure I proposed. I told Sun Aiqin that with RMB 2.5 million I would make a profit, and after the deal, there would be benefits for them. When negotiations were nearly settled, Sun Aiqin asked me to come out and sign the agreement together with Zhu Jinshun and the business manager of their company. I also told them I would not treat them badly. After the land transfer fee was transferred, I withdrew RMB 200,000 in cash and gave it to Sun Aiqin, asking him to distribute it among them.

2. Testimony of witness Zhu Jinshun, mainly to the effect: Around March-April 1993, I had just been transferred to Zhenhua Company as Deputy Director and was eager to complete some business. I approached Sun Aiqin and asked him to help make introductions. Since Sun was the Deputy Director of the Municipal Demolition Office, he knew many developers and had broad information. Sun introduced me to the plot at No. 8 Jiankang Road, saying it belonged to Liu Yijiang, and asked if I was interested. After contacting Liu, he said the land would cost RMB 2.5 million. I believed we could make a profit and thus accepted it and signed the agreement. Later, I heard from Sun Aiqin that Liu Yijiang had promised us a fee. I considered this a "kickback," but Sun Aiqin, Liu Yijiang, and I had not discussed taking a "kickback" beforehand. One evening, Sun Aiqin called me, and I went to Sun's home together with Wang Benxun from my company. Under Sun's building, Sun gave Wang and me RMB 50,000 each in cash, saying it was from Liu Yijiang, and that Liu had given a total of RMB 200,000. In developing this land, my company made a profit of over RMB 1 million, and Sun Aiqin played a role in introducing and facilitating the deal.

3. Testimony of witness Wang Benxun, mainly to the effect: During my tenure as Manager of the Business Department of Zhenhua Company, Zhu Jinshun asked me to assist him in handling the development of the plot at No. 8 Jiankang Road. One evening, Zhu Jinshun called me and asked me to go with him to Sun Aiqin's home. Sun gave a package to Zhu Jinshun. After going downstairs, Zhu took a stack of money from the package and gave it to me, telling me to hold it first, and I accepted it. Upon returning, I counted it as RMB 50,000. Later, I asked Zhu Jinshun what the RMB 50,000 was for. Zhu said it was from Liu Yijiang: Liu had obtained the land cheaply from the military, made money, and was distributing some. Zhu also said that Sun Aiqin had mediated the transfer of the land to our company and that Sun had also received money.

4. Testimony of witness Lu Guangyu, mainly to the effect: I had known Liu Yijiang for a long time; at that time, he was a demobilized soldier and said he planned to engage in real estate, asking me to help, and I agreed. I also knew Sun Aiqin for a long time, as we were in the same system. One day, Sun Aiqin told me that a friend of his wanted to do real estate but knew nothing and had no staff, and he wanted me to meet this person. Upon meeting, I realized it was Liu Yijiang. Liu said the military wanted to develop land and had already negotiated a plot with the military. He asked me to take a look. After seeing it, I told them the location was good and houses built there would sell easily. After Liu Yijiang obtained the approval from the military, Sun Aiqin told me to help Liu find a strong partner and suggested I contact Zhu Jinshun, whom I had worked with before. I introduced Liu Yijiang's project to Zhu Jinshun, and after hearing it, Zhu said we should discuss it. Later, a deal was struck. Sun Aiqin said to me, "Old Liu is generous; he said he won't treat us badly." One evening, Sun Aiqin called and asked me to come to his home. When I arrived, Liu Yijiang was also there. Sun Aiqin asked the two of us to go outside, and Liu Yijiang gave a bag to Sun Aiqin, saying, "Everything for you all is inside." I said, "What does this mean?" Liu said, "Wasn't this agreed upon beforehand? I keep my word, so don't be polite." With that, he left. Sun gave me RMB 50,000.

5. Confession of defendant Sun Aiqin, mainly to the effect: In the second half of 1993, Liu Yijiang obtained a plot from the military to develop commercial housing. But Liu lacked the qualifications and capability to develop. I was engaged in demolition work and was familiar with housing developers in Zhenjiang, so Liu asked me to find someone. I first found Lu Guangyu for him, but since Lu was unsuitable, I then found Zhu Jinshun, who thought the land was viable. During the negotiations among Zhu Jinshun, Wang Benxun, Lu Guangyu, and Liu Yijiang, I participated several times. When the formal negotiation of the land price occurred, Zhu Jinshun made a counteroffer, and Liu Yijiang said, "The land price is RMB 2.5 million. That's settled. I won't treat you all badly." I also chimed in, saying, "So be it." One evening, Liu Yijiang called me, indicating he wanted to give me money. He called me downstairs and gave me a plastic bag containing RMB 200,000. Later, I distributed RMB 50,000 each to Zhu Jinshun, Wang Benxun, and Lu Guangyu, keeping RMB 50,000 for myself.

6. Testimony of witness Liu Yijiang, mainly to the effect: Sun Aiqin used to be a neighbor of my elder brother Liu Yizhen. I got to know Sun Aiqin when I went to my brother's home to play cards, but we had no dealings then. During the development of the plot at No. 8 Jiankang Road, Sun Aiqin helped me find Zhu Jinshun. The plot at No. 17 Jiankang Road was jointly developed by me and the Military Region Cultural Station through an agreement. However, due to changes during development, the funds I had previously invested were not generating returns, so I asked Sun Aiqin to help contact Zhou Wei, the Director of Dantu Real Estate Bureau. At that time, I proposed that RMB 500,000 in funds were needed for cooperation on this plot, but Zhou Wei believed that RMB 300,000 would be sufficient to operate. I agreed that Zhou Wei would pay RMB 300,000 into my account, and they would proceed with development, construction, and sales. I would handle the economic dealings with the military. The cooperation with the Real Estate Bureau was very successful. For this reason, I asked Sun Aiqin and Zhou Wei to go to Shanghai with me, where I gave them RMB 100,000; the second time, I drove to the downstairs of Sun's home, called him out to my car, and gave him RMB 80,000. Whether Sun Aiqin shared this RMB 80,000 with Zhou Wei, I do not know. I gave Sun money, first, because he helped me find a cooperative development partner, and I wanted to express my gratitude; second, I very much wanted to befriend Sun Aiqin.

7. Testimony of witness Zhou Wei, mainly to the effect: At the beginning of 1994, I got to know Liu Yijiang through Sun Aiqin. After Sun Aiqin introduced us, I negotiated with Liu Yijiang regarding the joint development of the plot at No. 17 Jiankang Road. Sun Aiqin did not participate in those talks. On one occasion, Liu asked me and Sun Aiqin to go to Shanghai with him. After dinner at the hotel, when I was about to take a shower, Liu Yijiang entered the room occupied by me and Sun Aiqin, holding a package wrapped in newspaper, and said, "Take this money to buy something." I saw the package was quite large and knew it contained a significant amount of money, so I said, "For buying things, 10,000 or 20,000 yuan would be enough." Then I went to take a shower. When I came out of the shower, Sun Aiqin took five stacks of money (each stack of RMB 10,000) from under his blanket and gave them to me. At that time, I said to Sun, "You are just an introducer, so there's no problem. But I will still deal with Liu Yijiang regarding the development of this house. If he doesn't follow the agreement, it would be hard for my unit to explain. I'll just take RMB 20,000." Sun said it was fine and gave me RMB 50,000. Apart from these RMB 50,000, I had no other economic dealings with Liu Yijiang.

8. Confession of defendant Sun Aiqin, mainly to the effect: In 1994, Liu Yijiang obtained a second plot from the military and again asked me to find a development unit, saying he would not treat me badly. I helped him contact Zhou Wei. I participated in the negotiations; Liu Yijiang wanted a 50-50 split, while Zhou Wei wanted a 40-60 split. Liu Yijiang asked me to speak to Zhou Wei. After I spoke to Zhou Wei, the agreement was signed based on a 50-50 split. Thereafter, one day, Liu Yijiang asked me and Zhou Wei to go to Shanghai. At the hotel, in the presence of Zhou Wei, he handed me a plastic bag containing RMB 100,000 and said, "You two split this." At that time, Zhou Wei said to him, "Don't be so polite." That evening, I immediately gave Zhou Wei RMB 50,000. Three to four months after this incident, Liu Yijiang called me again and arranged to meet me downstairs at my home. In his car, he handed me a plastic bag containing RMB 80,000 in cash. Without even returning home, I went directly to Zhou Wei's home. At that time, his wife was at home. I did not give Zhou Wei RMB 40,000 in front of his wife. In my dealings with Liu Yijiang, I did not violate any principles to help him. I only visited his construction site several times during development to help resolve disputes with stubborn households resisting demolition.

The defendant Sun Aiqin argued: I only contacted developers for Liu Yijiang, as a private favor. I did not use my official position to assist Liu Yijiang in demolition or to seek any benefit. Moreover, my position at that time was only Deputy Director of the Demolition Office under the Development Office, so even if I wanted to help, I could not. Additionally, I did indeed give RMB 40,000 to Zhou Wei. As to the other facts alleged, I have no objection.

Sun Aiqin's defense counsel submitted: 1. Sun Aiqin and Zhu Jinshun did not share a common criminal intent, nor was there any joint criminal act. Sun Aiqin only acted as an introducer, and his conduct does not constitute the crime of bribery by company personnel. 2. Sun Aiqin and Zhou Wei did not share a common criminal intent, and objectively, Sun Aiqin did not participate in the transaction between Zhou Wei and Liu Yijiang. His conduct does not constitute the crime of bribery. 3. The fact that Sun Aiqin, after receiving the later RMB 80,000 from Liu Yijiang, transferred RMB 40,000 to Zhou Wei, was voluntarily disclosed by Sun Aiqin. There is no issue of admitting less serious conduct to conceal more serious conduct. Just because Zhou Wei does not admit it, it cannot be concluded that Sun Aiqin obtained all RMB 80,000.

The Jingkou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, after public trial, confirmed the other facts alleged by the prosecutorial authority as true, except that it found that the defendant Sun Aiqin appropriated only RMB 40,000 of Liu Yijiang's bribe of RMB 80,000 for himself.

The Jingkou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, held:

Regarding the whereabouts of the bribe of RMB 80,000 that the defendant Sun Aiqin received from Liu Yijiang, Sun Aiqin claimed that he gave RMB 40,000 to Zhou Wei, but Zhou Wei denied this. Apart from Sun Aiqin's confession and Zhou Wei's testimony, there is no other evidence to confirm this. Since there is a clear conflict of interest between Zhou Wei and Sun Aiqin, Zhou Wei's testimony cannot be accepted. Therefore, the prosecutorial authority's allegation that Sun Aiqin appropriated the entire RMB 80,000 for himself lacks sufficient evidence. Sun Aiqin's defense on this point should be accepted.

Article 163, paragraphs 1 and 2, of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, as revised on October 1, 1997, provides: "Where an employee of a company or enterprise, by taking advantage of his position, demands another person's property or illegally accepts another person's property and seeks benefits for that person, if the amount is relatively large, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; if the amount is huge, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years and may also be sentenced to confiscation of property." "Where an employee of a company or enterprise, in economic transactions, violates state regulations and accepts kickbacks or handling fees of various descriptions for his own benefit, he shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph." The crime under this article is named "bribery by company personnel."

Prior to the revision of the Criminal Law, Article 9 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing Crimes of Violating the Company Law provided: "Where a director, supervisor, or employee of a company, by taking advantage of his position, extorts or accepts bribes, if the amount is relatively large, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; if the amount is huge, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years and may also be sentenced to confiscation of property." The crime under this provision was named "commercial bribery." Article 14 of that Decision provided: "Where an employee of an enterprise other than a limited liability company or a company limited by shares commits a criminal act as specified in Articles 9, 10, or 11 of this Decision, this Decision shall apply."

The defendant Sun Aiqin, together with Zhu Jinshun and Zhou Wei, and by taking advantage of the official positions of Zhu and Zhou respectively, illegally accepted property from Liu Yijiang and sought benefits for Liu. His conduct violated the Criminal Law and constituted a joint crime. However, Sun Aiqin's conduct occurred before the implementation of the revised Criminal Law, and he should be convicted and sentenced in accordance with the 1979 Criminal Law and the Decision on Punishing Crimes of Violating the Company Law. Sun Aiqin's act of jointly accepting property from Liu Yijiang with Zhu Jinshun, taking advantage of Zhu's official position, should be found to constitute the crime of commercial bribery; Sun Aiqin's act of jointly accepting property from Liu Yijiang with Zhou Wei, taking advantage of Zhou's official position and seeking benefits for Liu, should be found to constitute the crime of bribery. Sun Aiqin committed two crimes and should be subject to concurrent punishment for multiple crimes. Sun Aiqin's criminal gains should be recovered according to law.

In summary, the Jingkou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, on November 15, 2001, rendered the following judgment:

1. The defendant Sun Aiqin is found guilty of commercial bribery and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of two years; guilty of bribery and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of eight years and six months, with confiscation of property of RMB 10,000. The combined sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of ten years, with confiscation of property of RMB 10,000.

2. The defendant Sun Aiqin's criminal gains of RMB 140,000 shall be recovered.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, the defendant Sun Aiqin appealed, arguing that he was not involved in a joint crime and that his conduct did not constitute the crimes of commercial bribery or bribery. Sun Aiqin's defense counsel also argued that Sun Aiqin's conduct should only be found to constitute the crime of introducing bribes, and that the statute of limitations for prosecution in this case had expired, so he should be acquitted.

The Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, after trial, held:

Regarding the second payment of RMB 80,000 in cash from Liu Yijiang to appellant Sun Aiqin arising from the development of the plot at No. 17 Jiankang Road, this is confirmed by Liu Yijiang's testimony and Sun Aiqin's confession and is sufficiently established. Sun Aiqin's confession that he transferred RMB 40,000 of this RMB 80,000 to Zhou Wei cannot be established on the basis of his confession alone. Accordingly, the facts found are as follows: In May 1994, through Sun Aiqin's introduction, Zhou Wei, Director of Dantu Real Estate Bureau, and Liu Yijiang, who was affiliated with Zhenhua Development Company, negotiated and jointly developed the plot at No. 17 Jiankang Road in Zhenjiang City. Thereafter, Liu Yijiang gave Sun Aiqin RMB 100,000, and Sun Aiqin immediately gave RMB 50,000 to Zhou Wei, keeping RMB 50,000 for himself. In October of the same year, Liu Yijiang again gave Sun Aiqin RMB 80,000. In addition, in April 1993, Sun Aiqin introduced and facilitated a joint development between Zhu Jinshun, Deputy Manager of Supply and Marketing Company, and Liu Yijiang concerning the plot at No. 8 Jiankang Road in Zhenjiang City, during which Sun Aiqin accepted RMB 50,000 in cash from Liu Yijiang.

Article 12, paragraph 1, of the revised Criminal Law provides: "Where an act committed after the founding of the People's Republic of China and before the implementation of this Law was not considered a crime under the laws at that time, the laws at that time shall apply. If the act was considered a crime under the laws at that time, and if prosecution is required under Section 8 of Chapter IV of the General Provisions of this Law, criminal liability shall be pursued under the laws at that time. However, if this Law does not consider the act a crime or imposes a lighter penalty, this Law shall apply." This case occurred before the implementation of the revised Criminal Law, so the provisions of the 1979 Criminal Law shall apply.

The 1979 Criminal Law did not criminalize bribery by employees of companies. Article 4 of the Supplementary Provisions on Punishing Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery, adopted at the 24th Session of the Standing Committee of the Sixth National People's Congress on January 21, 1988, provides: "Where a state functionary, an employee of a collective economic organization, or any other person engaged in public service, by taking advantage of his position, demands another person's property, or illegally accepts another person's property and seeks benefits for that person, is guilty of bribery." "Any person who colludes with a state functionary, an employee of a collective economic organization, or any other person engaged in public service and participates in bribery shall be punished as an accomplice." "Where a state functionary, an employee of a collective economic organization, or any other person engaged in public service, in economic transactions, violates state regulations and accepts kickbacks or handling fees of various descriptions for his own benefit, shall be punished as bribery."

The appellant Sun Aiqin, when Liu Yijiang asked him to help find a development unit, introduced and presented Liu Yijiang to Zhu Jinshun and Zhou Wei. After facilitating their joint development, Sun Aiqin accepted cash from Liu Yijiang and respectively transferred it to Zhu Jinshun, Zhou Wei, and others. Sun Aiqin did not conspire in advance with Zhu Jinshun and Zhou Wei to accept benefits from Liu Yijiang, nor did he conspire with Liu Yijiang to give gifts to Zhu and Zhou. Therefore, subjectively, he lacked both the intent to join in bribery with others and the intent to join in offering bribes with others. Objectively, Sun Aiqin only performed acts of introducing, communicating, and mediating between the bribe-giver and the bribe-taker. This was neither joint bribe-giving nor joint bribe-taking, but rather the introduction of bribes.

Zhu Jinshun was an employee of a collectively owned company. His acceptance of a kickback in the course of economic dealings should, under Article 4 of the Supplementary Provisions on Punishing Crimes of Corruption and Bribery, be treated as acceptance of bribes. However, under the revised Criminal Law, the subject of the crime of acceptance of bribes must be a state functionary. Since Zhu Jinshun was not a state functionary, his conduct could no longer constitute the crime of acceptance of bribes under the revised Criminal Law. Although the Decision on Punishing Crimes against the Company Law provides that "directors, supervisors, or employees of a company who, by taking advantage of their positions, demand or accept bribes of a relatively large amount" constitute the crime of commercial bribery, that Decision was promulgated and came into effect on February 28, 1995, and is not applicable to conduct that occurred in 1993. Since Zhu Jinshun's conduct of accepting a bribe from Liu Yijiang could not even constitute a crime, the appellant, Sun Aiqin, who introduced the bribe to him, naturally also did not constitute a crime. The first instance ruling that Sun Aiqin was an accomplice in the crime of commercial bribery was an error in the characterization of the crime.

Zhou Wei had the status of a state functionary. The appellant, Sun Aiqin, introduced a bribe to Zhou Wei, and his conduct violated the provisions of Article 185, Paragraph 3 of the 1979 Criminal Law, constituting the crime of introducing bribes, for which he should be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention. The RMB 50,000 he distributed to himself in the course of introducing the bribe constituted illegal gains.

Regardless of whether calculated under Article 76 of the 1979 Criminal Law or under Section 8 of Chapter 4 of the revised Criminal Law, a crime for which the maximum statutory punishment is fixed-term imprisonment of less than five years shall no longer be prosecuted after five years have elapsed. Article 77 of the 1979 Criminal Law further provides: "Where, after compulsory measures have been taken by a people's court, people's procuratorate, or public security organ, the criminal suspect evades investigation or trial, the limitation period for prosecution shall not apply." Article 78 provides: "The limitation period for prosecution shall run from the date the crime is committed; if the criminal act is continuous or continuing, it shall run from the date the criminal act is completed." "If another crime is committed during the limitation period for prosecution of the previous crime, the limitation period for prosecution of the previous crime shall run from the date the subsequent crime is committed." The appellant, Sun Aiqin, committed the crime of introducing bribes in June 1994 and was detained on June 21, 2001. During this period, Sun Aiqin was not subjected to any compulsory measures and did not commit any new crime. Under the 1979 Criminal Law, the five-year limitation period for prosecution for the crime of introducing bribes had already expired, and his criminal liability could no longer be pursued according to law. However, his illegal gains should be recovered according to law.

In summary, the appellant Sun Aiqin's grounds of appeal and the opinions of his defense counsel are supported by law and should be adopted. The first instance judgment finding Sun Aiqin guilty of the crime of commercial bribery and the crime of acceptance of bribes was an improper application of the law and should be corrected. Accordingly, the Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, pursuant to the provisions of Article 15, Item (2) and Article 162, Item (2) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on September 25, 2002, rendered the following judgment:

1. The criminal judgment of the first instance is reversed;

2. The appellant, Sun Aiqin, is found not guilty;

3. The illegal gains of the appellant, Sun Aiqin, in the amount of RMB 50,000, are to be confiscated.
